To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
3D chip multiprocessing with L2 memory networking provides better performance and power consumption than 2D designs.
a 3-D chip multiprocessor with a network-in-memory architecture is an attractive alternative to a 2D chip multiprocesser.

a network-in-memory L2 cache architecture with no dynamic migration of data between L2 cache layers generates much better performance and consumes less power than a 2-dimensional cache design with dynamic data migration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and management of 3D chip multi-processors using network-in-memory.
the design, management and optimization of L2 caches in a 3D chip-multiprocessor architecture.
the design of 3D L1 and L2 caches and the design of an embedded network in the L2 memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 3D design is a viable option for future chip multiprocessors, especially when it comes to the design of large L2 caches, and that a network-in-memory architecture is a good option to consider for future 3D chip multiprocessing systems.
a 3d architecture with no dynamic migration can outperform a conventional 2D design.
3D chip multiprocessing is a very attractive option for future high-performance and power-efficient systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 3-D L2 cache architecture is more scalable and power efficient than a 2-D L2 cache, especially when the number of layers and inter-wafer connections are large.
the 3D architecture is an effective solution for L2 design in chip multiprocessors, especially in the case when the interconnects between layers are not too expensive.
a network-based L2 cache design with no data migration is a good design choice for 3D chip multiprocessing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3D architectures are promising for L2 designs, and that they can be used in conjunction with a network-in-memory to achieve significant performance and energy benefits over 2D designs.
3D L1 and L2 cache designs are a viable option to improve system performance and power efficiency.

3D architectures can be designed in such a way as to provide significant advantages in terms of power and performance, and that these advantages are even more pronounced in 3D architectures that do not require dynamic data migration in L2 caches.
